messages:
maria.k: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (prefer-attn-fast on short seqs) we're seeing host-side overhead rise on streaming requests. Latency tail jumped ~12-18ms P95 on small chat messages.
chen: saw that in the dashboards too. was it the kernel swap or the new batching hint?
maria.k: kernel swap + the auto-batcher started grouping tiny streaming frames into 2-3 token aggregates. suspect extra parse/serialize cycles + writev churn. attached profiler snippet: 
```
host_parse -> 1.9ms
serialize_chunk -> 3.2ms
grpc_writev -> 4.6ms
kv_cache_lookup -> 0.4ms
total extra -> ~9.1ms
```
alex: interesting — writev is big. are we coalescing incorrectly for http2/grpc streams?
sam: quick note: the kernel change reduced decode time for long seqs so overall token CPU went down, but overhead moved to ingress path.
chen: can we toggle the batching hint to never coalesce streaming subframes <16 bytes? that'd reduce writev calls.
maria.k: tried a canary: disabled coalesce for streaming routes -> P95 dropped 14ms, but CPU on host up a tiny bit since we lost aggregation. tradeoff looks honest.
alex: what about prefix/KV caching interactions — if we trigger KV lookup per tiny frame it might thrash hot shards. profiler shows kv_cache_lookup spikes on certain clients.
sam: yes, saw kv_hot_shard on 3 instances. likely from many tiny user messages hitting the same context id. we should debounce kv_lookup in the ingress pipeline for streaming.
chen: idea: add a tiny micro-batch window (3-5ms) for streaming parses only when latency SLOs allow — should preserve writev/coalesce benefits without 100% aggregation.
maria.k: good call. let's prototype a 4ms debounce in ingress parser, and add a flag to force immediate flush for low-latency routes. I'll open a canary PR.
alex: also check grpc options: set `GRPC_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE` and `SO_SNDBUF` knobs in sidecar; on some nodes writev latency correlates with kernel socket buffer backpressure.
sam: +1. add alerts for writev latency > 5ms per request and kv_lookup rate > 200/s per shard.
maria.k: created PR 5987 — canary on dev cluster (tag: host-opt/token-debounce). deploy-bot: Deploy queued — running canary on dev/eng-runtime (3 pods).
chen: running load test now with 1000 small streaming chats, will post numbers in 10m.
alex: if canary looks good we should roll to dedicated pool first before global. also add perf regression test to CI that measures P95 for 1-4 token streaming payloads.
maria.k: agreed. thanks all — will gather profiler traces after canary and post results. :thumbsup:
